source_text: Καὶ ὤνησαν οὐδὲν μέχρι νῦν γράφοντες, ἐξαλείφοντες, βιαζόμενοι, οὐκ εἰδότες, ὅτι Πᾶσα μὲν φυτεία, ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος, ἐκριζωθήσεται τὸ δὲ ῥῆμα τοῦ Κυρίου τὸ διὰ τῆς οἰκουμενικῆς συνόδου ἐν τῇ Νικαίᾳ γενόμενον μέ νει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα. Ἄν τε γὰρ ἀριθμὸν ἀριθμῷ τις συμβάλῃ, πλείους οἱ ἐν Νικαίᾳ τῶν κατὰ μέρος εἰσὶν, ὅσον καὶ τὸ ὅλον πλεῖόν ἐστι τοῦ μέρους ἄν τε τὸ αἴτιον τῆς ἐν Νικαίᾳ καὶ τῶν μετ' αὐτὴν τοσούτων γενομένων συνόδων παρὰ τούτων διαγνῶναι τις ἐθέλοι, εὕροι ἂν τὴν μὲν ἐν Νικαίᾳ ἔχουσαν τὸ αἴτιον εὔλογον, τὰς δὲ ἄλλας διὰ μῖσος καὶ φιλονεικίαν ἐκ βίας συγκροτηθείσας. Ἡ μὲν γὰρ διὸ τὴν Ἀρειανὴν αἵρεσιν καὶ διὰ τὸ Πάσχα συνήχθη· ἐπειδὴ οἱ κατὰ Συρίαν, καὶ Κιλικίαν, καὶ Μεσοποταμίαν διεφώνουν πρὸς ἡμᾶς, καὶ τῷ καιρῷ, ἐν ᾧ ποιοῦσιν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, ἐποίουν καὶ αὐτοί. Ἀλλὰ χάρις τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὥσπερ περὶ τῆς πίστεως, οὕτω καὶ περὶ τῆς ἁγίας ἑορτῆς γέγονε συμφωνία. Καὶ τοῦτο ἦν τὸ αἴτιον τῆς ἐν Νικαίᾳ συνόδου· αἱ δὲ μετὰ ταύτην ὑπὲρ ἀριθμὸν μὲν, κατὰ δὲ τῆς οἰκουμενικῆς συνόδου ἐπενοήθησαν. Τούτων δὲ οὕτω δεικνυμένων, τίς ἀποδέξεται τοὺς τὴν Ἀρίμηνον ἢ ἄλλην σύνοδον παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ ὀνομάζοντας; ἢ τίς οὐκ ἂν μισήσειε τοὺς ἀθετοῦντας μὲν τὰ τῶν Πατέρων, τὰ δὲ νεώτερα ἐν τῇ Ἀριμήνῳ κατὰ φιλονεικίαν καὶ βίαν συντιθέντα προκρίνοντας; Τίς δὲ τούτοις συνελθεῖν ἐθελήσοι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, μηδὲ τὰ ἑαυτῶν ἀποδεχομένοις; Οἱ γὰρ ἐν ταῖς ἑαυτῶν δέκα που καὶ πλέον, καθὰ προείπαμεν, συνόδοις, ἄλλοτε ἄλλα γράφοντες, δῆλοί εἰσιν ἑκάστης αὐτοὶ κατήγοροι γινόμενοι. Πάσχουσι δέ τι τοιοῦτον, οἷον καὶ οἱ τότε τῶν Ἰουδαίων προδόται πεπόνθασιν· ὡς γὰρ ἐκεῖνοι, καταλείψαντες τὴν μόνην πηγὴν τοῦ ζῶντος ὕδατος, ὤρυξαν ἑαυτοῖς λάκκους συντετριμμένους, οἳ οὐ δυνήσονται ὕδωρ συνέχειν, γέγραπται δὲ τοῦτο παρὰ τῷ προφήτῃ Ἱερεμίᾳ· οὕ τως οὗτοι, μαχόμενοι πρὸς τὴν μίαν καὶ οἰκουμενικὴν σύνοδον, ὤρυξαν ἑαυτοῖς συνόδους πολλάς· καὶ πᾶσαι κεναὶ, αἳ παρ' αὐτοῖς ὡς δράγμα μὴ ἔχων ἰσχὺν ἐφάνησαν. Μὴ τοίνυν ἀνεχώμεθα τῶν τὴν Ἀρίμηνον ἢ ἄλλην ὀνομαζόντων σύνοδον παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νι καίᾳ γενομένην. Καὶ γὰρ καὶ αὐτοὶ οἱ τὴν Ἀρίμηνον ὀνομάζοντες ἐοίκασι μὴ εἰδέναι τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ πραχθέντα· ἢ γὰρ ἂν ἐσιώπησαν. Οἴδατε γὰρ, ἀγαπητοὶ, μαθόντες καὶ ὑμεῖς παρὰ τῶν ἐλθόντων ἐξ ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν Ἀρίμηνον, ὡς Οὐρσάκιος καὶ Οὐάλης, Εὐδόξιος καὶ Αὐξέντιος, ἐκεῖ δὲ ἦν σὺν αὐτοῖς καὶ Δημόφιλος, καθῃρέθησαν, θελήσαντες ἕτερα παρὰ τὰ ἐν Νικαίᾳ γράφειν· ὅτε καὶ ἀπαιτηθέντες ἀναθεματίσαι τὴν Ἀρειανὴν αἵρεσιν, παρῃτήσαντο, καὶ μᾶλλον αὐτῆς ἤθελον εἶναι προστάται. Οἱ δέ γε ἐπίσκοποι, οἱ ἀληθῶς γνήσιοι δοῦλοι τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ὀρθῶς πιστεύοντες, ἦσαν δὲ ἐγγὺς διακόσιοι, ἔγραψαν ἀρκεῖσθαι τῇ ἐν Νικαίᾳ μόνῃ, καὶ μηδὲν πλέον ἢ ἔλαττον παρ' ἐκεί νην ζητεῖν ἢ φρονεῖν. Ταῦτα καὶ Κωνσταντίῳ δεδηλώκασι, τῷ καὶ τὴν σύνοδον κελεύσαντι γενέσθαι. Ἀλλ' οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀριμήνῳ καθαιρεθέντες, ἀπελθόντες πρὸς Κωνστάντιον, πεποιήκασιν ὑβρισθῆναι μὲν, ἀπειλὰς δὲ γενέσθαι, μὴ ἀνακάμψειν εἰς τὰς ἰδίας παροικίας τοὺς κατ' αὐτῶν ἀποφηναμένους, βίαν τε παθεῖν ἐν τῇ Θρᾴκῃ ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ χειμῶνι· ὥστε τῶν παρ' αὐτῶν καινοτομουμένων ἀνέχεσθαι.
thought_title: Nicaea endures; later councils are empty
orientation: Athanasius is writing to the bishops of Africa, arguing that the Nicene Council is the one sufficient ecumenical council and that later councils, especially Ariminum, were contrived by Arians out of rivalry and violence.
pass_a_gloss: And they have profited nothing until now by writing, by erasing, by using force, not knowing that 'Every plant which the heavenly Father did not plant will be rooted out,' but the word of the Lord which came about through the ecumenical council in Nicaea remains forever. For if someone compares number with number, those in Nicaea are more than those in the partial ones, as much as the whole is more than the part; and if someone wishes to discern from these people the cause of the council in Nicaea and of the so many councils that happened after it, he would find that the one in Nicaea has a reasonable cause, but the others were assembled through hatred and rivalry out of violence. For the one was gathered because of the Arian heresy and because of the Passover; since those throughout Syria and Cilicia and Mesopotamia were in disagreement with us, and at the time in which the Jews do it, they also did it. But thanks be to the Lord, just as concerning the faith, so also concerning the holy feast agreement came about. And this was the cause of the council in Nicaea; but the ones after it were devised beyond number, and against the ecumenical council. Since these things are shown in this way, who will accept those who name Ariminum or another council besides the one in Nicaea? Or who would not hate those who reject the things of the Fathers, and prefer the newer things composed in Ariminum through rivalry and force? And who will wish to assemble with these men, who do not even accept their own things? For those who in their own ten or more councils, as we said before, write different things at different times, are clearly becoming accusers of each one themselves. And they suffer something such as also the traitors of the Jews then suffered; for as those, having abandoned the only fountain of living water, dug for themselves broken cisterns which will not be able to hold water, and this is written in the prophet Jeremiah; so these men, fighting against the one and ecumenical council, dug for themselves many councils; and all are empty, which among them appeared like straw having no strength. Therefore let us not put up with those who name Ariminum or another council besides the one that happened in Nicaea. For indeed also those who name Ariminum seem not to know the things done in it; for otherwise they would have been silent. For you know, beloved, having learned also yourselves from those who came from you to Ariminum, how Ursacius and Valens, Eudoxius and Auxentius, and Demophilus was there with them, were deposed, having wished to write other things besides the things in Nicaea; when also having been required to anathematize the Arian heresy, they refused, and rather wished to be its champions. But the bishops, the truly genuine servants of the Lord and believing rightly, and they were about two hundred, wrote that they were content with the one in Nicaea alone, and to seek or think nothing more or less besides that one. These things they also made known to Constantius, who had also ordered the council to happen. But those deposed in Ariminum, having gone to Constantius, caused insults to happen, and threats to occur, that those who had voted against them would not return to their own parishes, and that they would suffer violence in Thrace in the very winter; so that they would put up with the innovations made by them.

choices.why: The verb ὀνίνημι means to profit or benefit; the aorist with μέχρι νῦν expresses completed action up to the present.
The verb means to wipe out or erase, referring to their altering of earlier council decisions.

choices.english: but the word of the Lord
choices.why: ῥῆμα means spoken word or utterance; the contrast with the plant that will be rooted out is preserved.
The phrase means 'in part' or 'partial,' contrasting local councils with the whole ecumenical council.
The prepositional phrase indicates the means or source; βία means force or violence.
δράγμα means straw or stubble, not a bound sheaf; the image is of worthless, weak straw.
rejected: like a sheaf that has no strength

pass_b_english: And they have profited nothing up to now by writing, erasing, and using force, not knowing that "Every plant that the heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted out" (Matthew 15:13), but the word of the Lord that came through the ecumenical council at Nicaea remains forever. For if someone compares number with number, those at Nicaea are more than the partial ones, just as the whole is greater than the part. And if someone wishes to discern the reason for the council at Nicaea and for the many councils that came after it from these people, he would find that the one at Nicaea had a reasonable cause, while the others were assembled out of hatred and rivalry by violence. For the one was gathered because of the Arian heresy and because of the Passover, since those in Syria, Cilicia, and Mesopotamia were in disagreement with us and were celebrating at the same time as the Jews. But thanks be to the Lord, just as concerning the faith, so also concerning the holy feast there came to be agreement. And this was the reason for the council at Nicaea. But the ones after it were beyond number, and they were devised against the ecumenical council. Since these things are so clearly shown, who will accept those who name Ariminum or another council alongside the one at Nicaea? Or who would not hate those who reject the things of the Fathers and prefer the newer things composed at Ariminum out of rivalry and violence? Who would wish to assemble with these men, who do not even accept their own decisions? For in their own ten or more councils, as we said before, they wrote different things at different times, and they are clearly becoming accusers of each one of them. They suffer something like what the traitors among the Jews suffered then. For as those men, abandoning the only fountain of living water, dug for themselves broken cisterns that cannot hold water—and this is written in the prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 2:13)—so these men, fighting against the one ecumenical council, dug for themselves many councils, and all of them appeared among them as empty, like a sheaf with no strength. Let us not, then, put up with those who name Ariminum or another council alongside the one that took place at Nicaea. For even those who name Ariminum seem not to know what was done there; otherwise they would have been silent. For you know, beloved, having learned also from those who came from you to Ariminum, that Ursacius and Valens, Eudoxius and Auxentius—and Demophilus was there with them—were deposed when they wanted to write things other than those at Nicaea. When they were required to anathematize the Arian heresy, they refused and preferred to be its champions. But the bishops who were truly genuine servants of the Lord and believed rightly—there were about two hundred of them—wrote that they were satisfied with Nicaea alone and sought or thought nothing more or less than that. They made this clear also to Constantius, who had ordered the council to take place. But those who were deposed at Ariminum went to Constantius and caused insults to occur and threats to be made that those who had voted against them would not return to their own districts, and they caused those bishops to suffer violence in Thrace in the dead of winter, so that they would put up with the innovations made by the deposed men.

problems.quote: that they would suffer violence in Thrace in the very winter, so that they would put up with the innovations made by them
problems.source_quote: βίαν τε παθεῖν ἐν τῇ Θρᾴκῃ ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ χειμῶνι· ὥστε τῶν παρ' αὐτῶν καινοτομουμένων ἀνέχεσθαι
problems.why: The subject shifts: the deposed Arians caused threats that the orthodox bishops would suffer violence, so that the orthodox would put up with the Arians' innovations. English 'they would suffer' is ambiguous about who suffers and who innovates.
problems.fix: that the bishops would suffer violence in Thrace in the very winter, so that they would endure the innovations of the deposed men
problems.ruling: Ambiguous 'they' obscures that orthodox bishops suffer violence so they tolerate Arians' innovations; reader misled on agency.

edits.old: that they would suffer violence in Thrace in the very winter, so that they would put up with the innovations made by them
edits.new: that the bishops would suffer violence in Thrace in the very winter, so that they would put up with the innovations made by the deposed men

fixed: The source βίαν τε παθεῖν refers to the orthodox bishops who voted against the Arians, not the Arians themselves; clarified the subject as 'the bishops' and 'the deposed men' for the innovators.

problems.why: 'each one' misrepresents ἑκάστης (feminine genitive singular), referring to 'each council' (συνόδου), not persons.
problems.fix: they wrote different things at different times, and they are clearly becoming accusers of each one of them
problems.ruling: ἑκάστης (fem. gen. sing.) refers to each council (συνόδῳ), not 'each one' of persons; meaning is obscured.

fixed: Corrected 'each one' to 'each one of them' to reflect that ἑκάστης refers to each council (συνόδου), not persons.

problems.quote: Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted
problems.source_quote: Πᾶσα μὲν φυτεία, ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος
problems.why: Source says 'the heavenly Father' without 'my'; 'my' changes the quote and adds words not in source.
problems.fix: Every plant that the heavenly Father has not planted
problems.ruling: Source lacks μου; 'my' alters the quotation from Matthew 15:13.

problems.source_quote: αἳ παρ' αὐτοῖς ὡς δράγμα μὴ ἔχων ἰσχὺν ἐφάνησαν
problems.why: δράγμα means 'a drachma' (a small coin), not 'straw'; the point is worthlessness, not material.
problems.fix: which appeared among them like a drachma, having no strength
problems.ruling: δράγμα means 'handful/sheaf,' not 'drachma' or 'straw'; 'straw' misleads on material.

problems.quote: that the bishops would suffer violence in Thrace
problems.source_quote: βίαν τε παθεῖν ἐν τῇ Θρᾴκῃ
problems.why: The Greek says 'that they [the deposed men] would suffer violence,' not 'the bishops'; subject is the deposed, not the orthodox.
problems.fix: that they themselves would suffer violence in Thrace
problems.ruling: βίαν τε παθεῖν lacks explicit subject; 'the bishops' wrongly specifies, potentially misleading reader.
